Export an ATAC object and explicit result/resource tables

Source: R/ExportATACResults.R
ExportATACResults.Rd

Save the complete object, supplied result tables and external resource inventory in a new directory with file checksums.

Usage

ExportATACResults(
  object,
  outdir,
  assay = NULL,
  tables = list(),
  counts = FALSE,
  compress = TRUE
)

Arguments

object

A validated Seurat ChromatinAssay object.

outdir

A new output directory. Existing paths are never overwritten.

assay

Source chromatin assay; defaults to the active assay.

tables

Uniquely named list of data frames, such as complete DAR tests, design/contrast tables, motif enrichment or peak annotation. Names must be safe filenames composed of letters, numbers, dots, underscores or hyphens, unique even when compared case-insensitively.

counts

Whether to additionally write the sparse peak counts as Matrix Market. The full object RDS always retains its assays and analysis results.

compress

Compression passed to saveRDS for the complete object.

Value

Invisibly, a list with the normalized directory, export file manifest and validation report. Tables are exported as supplied, without filtering.

Details

The output contains object.rds, cells.csv, peaks.bed (0-based half-open), fragments.csv, fragment_cells.csv, check.rds, sessionInfo.txt, supplied result tables and a file manifest with MD5 checksums. Fragments and reference genomes remain external; no automatic copying, downloading or path repair occurs. The BED has three columns and, with counts.mtx and barcodes.tsv when counts = TRUE, can be read by ReadATACData() when the selected assay satisfies its native minimum of two peaks and two cells. Smaller subsets can still be restored from object.rds. cells.csv and barcodes.tsv contain the selected assay cells in matrix column order. object.rds preserves all assays and cells. CSV files preserve values, not R column classes. The fragment column joins fragment_cells.csv to fragments.csv. The resource table retains inactive resources, with active marking current assay use; n_cells is the attached mapping size, not the exported cell count. Missing fragment files do not prevent a valid matrix-only export. Stored Signac resource hashes are labeled as such, and resource availability is only a snapshot. After moving resources, explicitly update paths with native Signac UpdatePath and rerun CheckATACData before fragment-dependent computations. Files are staged in the destination parent and moved to the requested new directory only after all writes succeed. This does not modify the object.

Examples

counts <- Matrix::sparseMatrix(
  i = c(1, 2, 1), j = c(1, 2, 2), x = c(2, 3, 1), dims = c(2, 2),
  dimnames = list(c("p1", "p2"), c("cell1", "cell2"))
)
ranges <- GenomicRanges::GRanges(c("chr1:1-50", "chr1:101-150"))
object <- ReadATACData(counts, ranges = ranges, genome = "hg38")
destination <- tempfile("atac-export-")
result <- ExportATACResults(object, destination, counts = TRUE)
result$manifest$file
#>  [1] "README.txt"         "barcodes.tsv"       "cells.csv"         
#>  [4] "check.rds"          "counts.mtx"         "fragment_cells.csv"
#>  [7] "fragments.csv"      "object.rds"         "peaks.bed"         
#> [10] "sessionInfo.txt"   
restored <- readRDS(file.path(destination, "object.rds"))
CheckATACData(restored)$valid
#> [1] TRUE
matrix_only <- ReadATACData(file.path(destination, "counts.mtx"),
  peaks.file = file.path(destination, "peaks.bed"),
  barcodes.file = file.path(destination, "barcodes.tsv"), genome = "hg38"
)
CheckATACData(matrix_only)$valid
#> [1] TRUE
unlink(destination, recursive = TRUE)
